subject: Operations
title: 3D Printing and Additive Manufacturing
description: A 60-second lesson on 3D Printing and Additive Manufacturing.

hook.text: A hospital prints a custom titanium hip implant in 8 hours. No mold. No minimum order. Just a file and a printer.

buildup.text: 3D printing builds objects layer by layer from digital designs—eliminating molds, tooling, and minimum batch sizes.

discovery.text: It enables mass customization, on-demand spare parts, and rapid prototyping at a fraction of traditional cost.

twist.text: 3D printing is still slower than injection molding for mass production. It excels at low-volume, high-complexity items.

climax.text: SpaceX 3D-prints rocket engine components that would take months to machine—reducing parts, weight, and cost.

punchline.text: Print what you need, when you need it, where you need it.

quiz.question: Where does 3D printing excel over traditional manufacturing?
